title: Pasar a: Moving On to the Next Step

sections.content:
You know *empezar a* + infinitive from A2 Unit 28. *Pasar a* + infinitive also starts an action, but it adds an idea that *empezar a* does not have: something came before, and now you move on to the next step. It does not mean "to pass".

You hear it in talks and meetings (*Ahora pasemos a ver los resultados*), and it also describes a change of role or situation (*pasó a dirigir la oficina*, "went on to run the office"). With *ser* it means "went on to be": *pasó a ser* the director.

sections.title: pasar a + infinitive
rows: Ahora pasemos a ver los resultados.
Now let us move on to the results.
Terminó el primer ejercicio y pasó a hacer el segundo.
She finished the first exercise and moved on to the second.
Después de varios años, pasó a dirigir la oficina.
After several years, he went on to run the office.
Después de la cena, pasamos a hablar del viaje.
After dinner, we moved on to talk about the trip.

sections.content: *Pasar a* needs a first step to move on from. If nothing came before, use *empezar a*: *Empecé a estudiar español hace un año*, not *Pasé a estudiar*.
